Every clause of Lemma 5.1 is stated. Existence for all positive orders on one radial interval and one parameter neighbourhood, with zero axis values, smoothness in X through the axis and holomorphy in eta of every fixed radial derivative, is SlowRecursion.exists_local_slow_hierarchy, instantiated on the actual analytic axis profile by ActualSlowAxis.fromNatural_*; the equations it imposes are (5.2)-(5.6) term by term once K_n is identified with the average defect. Uniqueness is PositiveAxisDifferential.positive_solution_unique, stated for the equivalent first-order system (5.7) exactly as the paper's own proof does, in a class that differs from the paper's only by continuity in place of uniform bounds. The differences I found are encoding and packaging, so different_formulation and OK.

findings.summary: Uniqueness is stated for the equivalent six-component system (5.7) with zero axis data, not for quadruples solving (5.2)-(5.6); no single declaration conjoins existence and uniqueness for a positive order.

The Lean comparison class asks joint continuity on [0,a] x U and vanishing of all six components at the axis, where the paper asks only for \eta-holomorphy with bounds uniform in \xi and zero axis data for \phi_n, U_n, \Pi_n.
The Lean system carries an auxiliary unknown K_n with the row X(U_n'+K_n')+K_n=0 in place of the radial average A_X(U_n) of (5.2).
The clause locating the interval inside the collar where the stress cone inequalities hold with a uniform positive margin is attached to no declaration of this construction.

Lean gives one parameter neighbourhood serving every order and every radial derivative, where the paper allows the neighbourhood and the bounds to shrink with both. The Lean statement is the stronger one.
